messages:
mike: heads-up, ran into an assert in allocator drain during the new prefetch stress run. dumping notes here so it's in one place

tara: which assert? paste stack?

mike: "drain: no outstanding reservations allowed" at alloc.cc:421
stack:
```
#0 0x7f8c1a2b drain()
#1 0x7f8c1a7e prefetch_completion_cb()
#2 0x7f8c1b00 worker_thread()
```
repro: staging stress harness: `./tools/prefetch_stress --clients=200 --seq=8192`

jia: was there a CI/unit repro or only staging?

mike: only on staging so far, flaky. I added a tiny harness that toggles prefetch and it flakes reliably in ~1h. link: https://staging/logs/174871-prefetch (internal)

sam: remind me of the ownership: who holds the reservation lifecycle during prefetch callback?

mike: flow is: request -> reserve pages via alloc API -> issue prefetch IO -> prefetch completion runs callback which may touch allocator state and release reservation. drain waits for reservations to be released. Seems callback sometimes releases after drain already checked, causing assert.

tara: could be missing refcount bump when handing callback to worker thread. callback should either own or borrow the reservation ref.

mike: I instrumented refcounts; sequence we see is 1 -> 0 inside callback, but drain snapshot sees 0 and asserts. race window small but appears under heavy contention.

jia: one fix: callback increments a short-lived "callback-hold" ref at entry and decrements at exit. drain should observe that.

sam: we already have an inflight IO counter separate from reservation refs. We could make drain check both. Simpler but may still have snapshot races.

tara: snapshot race is the issue. drain might read counters before callback increments. We need a handshake: drain sets a draining flag, callbacks check the flag and if set they must increment an "ongoing-callbacks" counter under an atomic path that drain will wait on.

mike: two-phase drain: 1) set draining flag 2) wait for ongoing-callbacks==0. callbacks do: if (!draining) proceed; else atomically increment ongoing-callbacks then double-check. If they see drain in progress after increment, they continue and decrement on exit. Guarantees no callback runs completely unseen.

sam: that is handshaking. Cost?

mike: microbench: if drains are rare, negligible. Under pathological frequent drain it adds ~0.2% p50 latency. acceptable for safety.

jia: longer term we should always require a lightweight lease for any path touching allocator state — unify with compaction/eviction invariants. This handshake is a tactical fix.

tara: agree. For short-term: implement draining flag + callback handoff counter + unit test that forces race. Add telemetry: drain_attempts, average wait, callbacks_seen_during_drain.

mike: plan for PR:
- add atomic draining flag to allocator
- callbacks check flag and inc/dec ongoing-callbacks when needed
- drain sets flag then waits on ongoing-callbacks==0 and legacy refs==0
- add unit test that spins worker threads to repro race and asserts no crash
- add tracepoints and telemetry counters
- add experimental feature-flag to rollback behavior in canary

sam: add a canary rollout gate and a kill-switch config in case of issues. also include backtrace sampling in traces when drain waits > 10ms.

mike: will do. opening PR today. tagging @sam for review.

infra-bot: scheduled canary rollout for branch mike/prefetch-drain-fix on cluster:staging-canary at 2026-04-02T09:00Z :white_check_mark:

jia: I'll follow up with a compaction integration test matrix (prefetch + compaction + drain).

tara: also add a debug log when drain starts/ends with sample of counters (only when debug_trace enabled). helped diagnose before.

mike: good call, adding tracepoints + short doc in PR. will paste link when ready.

sam: thanks, appreciate the quick triage.

mike: thanks all, closing this thread once PR is up.
